#en: Out in this thin band of orbit, the stars feel slightly out of place, like someone has been tugging the sky a few degrees at a time. The sensor hub anchored here drinks in stray radiation no one bothers to catalogue, then quietly nudges jump plots by fractions, enough to send whole convoys skimming a different stretch of dark. Whatever has been watching the lanes from this vantage has been doing it for a long time, long enough that course corrections and "harmless" detours have started to stack into a pattern nobody will admit seeing. From a forgotten slate on a frontier rock, to convoy reports that all blamed the same phantom malfunction, to a derelict node full of stolen Fleet math, every fragment I have touched points toward someone mapping a second set of routes underneath the official ones, as if the Settled Systems have been walking in their sleep along a path they never chose.
zh: 在这条稀薄的轨道带上，群星感觉略有错位，像有人一直在一次几度地拽动天空。锚定于此的传感器中枢啜饮着没人费心编目的游离辐射，然后把跃迁图悄悄推偏几个零头——足以让整支车队贴着另一段黑暗掠过。无论是什么从这个视角监视航道，它都做了很久，久到航向修正与"无害"绕行开始堆叠成一个没人愿意承认自己看见过的模式。从边境岩石上一块被遗忘的数据板，到全都归咎于同一"幽灵故障"的车队报告，再到一座塞满偷来的舰队数学的废弃节点，我碰过的每一块碎片都指向有人在官方航线之下绘制第二套路线，仿佛定居星系一直在睡梦中沿着一条他们从未选择的路径行走。

#en: The UC warship hanging cold in the dark is where the patterns finally start to line up; only a combat ship with classified telemetry and sealed routing orders could carry the kind of navigational truth everyone else has been careful to obscure behind jargon, half-redacted reports, and convenient memory lapses. Its designation still whispers authority, even as the hull scars and powered-down guns say it was written out of the official story, a perfect vault for records nobody wants to acknowledge exist. Here, buried in Navy systems, is where whispers about bad drives, missing recalls, and engineered failures either converge into something solid or dissolve into sanctioned amnesia. So far the trail runs like this: a stray slate in the dust, scattered logs in a lonely outpost, glitching data on a small, drifting hull, and now a warship whose silence says more than any testimony ever has.
zh: 那艘冷寂地悬在黑暗中的联殖军舰，是这些模式终于开始对齐的地方；只有一艘带着机密遥测与密封路由命令的战斗舰，才可能承载那种别人都小心翼翼地用术语、半涂黑报告与"方便的记忆空白"掩盖起来的导航真相。它的编号仍在低语着权威，即便船壳上的伤痕与断电的枪炮说明它已被写出了官方故事——一件存放"没人愿意承认存在之记录"的完美保险库。在这里、埋在海军系统里的某处，关于坏引擎、失踪召回与被人为制造的故障的低语，要么汇聚成某种坚实之物，要么消散成获批的失忆。目前为止，线索是这样的：尘土里一块散落数据板、一座孤独前哨里零散的日志、一具小而漂移的船壳上闪故障的数据，如今又是一艘沉默比任何证词都说得更多的军舰。

#en: Only in the quiet between planets could she afford to be careless, stashing her trail in the shadow of a drifting hull and trusting that no one would look twice at another dead ship in a busy grav lane. Out here, far from city sensors and frontier gossip, familiar routines do the hiding for her: patrols skim past on autopilot, haulers file their standard reports, and yet one vessel hangs slightly off its declared vector, its systems humming just enough to keep a buried grid alive. Crack this shell and the pattern she has been flying suddenly has a spine, a plotted route back to the place she erased from every official record. So far the trail has been fragments and afterthoughts a stray slate in the back country, altered logs from a ruined farm, a nervous broker on Neon, a broken survey cutter full of curses and half a jump plan all pointing toward something she once called Hearthline.
zh: 只有在行星之间的安静里，她才负担得起粗心：把痕迹藏在某具漂移船壳的阴影下，并笃信没人会对一条繁忙引力航道里又一艘死船多看一眼。在这里，远离城市传感器与边境闲话，熟悉的惯例替她藏身：巡逻队在自动驾驶下掠过、货船提交标准报告，而偏偏有一艘船微微偏离它申报的向量，系统嗡鸣得刚好够让一张被埋的电网存活。撬开这具外壳，她一直飞行的模式就突然有了脊柱，一条绘回她从所有官方记录上抹掉之处的路线。目前为止，这条线索是碎片与事后的想法：乡间一块散落数据板、一座毁坏农场上被改动的日志、霓虹城一名紧张的掮客、一艘塞满咒骂与半份跃迁计划的破损勘探切割船，全都指向她一度称作"炉线"的东西。

#en: The science facility hangs in the dark like a sealed wound, its official Reliant Medical transponder the perfect mask for what has been growing inside. Here Stitch has everything he needs in one sterile shell: containment fields for unwilling donors, chem labs for his counter-formulas, servers to house every forbidden triage decision he ever logged. The stolen stimulants, vanished organ tags, and black-box data all converge on this lab, feeding a single, coherent design to break the scarcity he blames on UC and corporate hands. If he secures his archive and stabilizes his latest blends, that design spills uncontrolled across the Settled Systems. Back at the maintenance bay, the first hint was a too-clean table and missing chems; at the blood-slick track, whispers and doctored logs proved he was still practicing, just out of sight of those who swear they saw nothing worth worrying about.
zh: 那座科研设施像一道封住的伤口悬在黑暗中，它官方"信实医疗"的应答器为内部正在滋长的一切提供了完美的面具。在这里，"缝合"在一个无菌外壳里拥有了他需要的一切：为不自愿供体准备的隔离场、为他那些对抗配方准备的化学实验室、以及存放他记录过的每一次禁忌分诊决策的服务器。被盗的兴奋剂、消失的器官标签与黑匣数据全都汇聚到这座实验室，喂养着一个单一而连贯的设计——用来打破他归咎于联殖与公司之手的稀缺。若他保住自己的档案并稳定最新配方，那个设计就会不受控地溢满定居星系。回到那间维修舱，第一条线索是一张干净得过分的桌子与失踪的药剂；在血迹黏滑的赛道上，低语与被做手脚的日志证明他仍在行医，只是离开了那些发誓"没看见任何值得担心之事"之人的视线。

#en: Out here the research module hangs quiet over nothing much at all, exactly the kind of place bureaucrats forget and contractors exploit. This is where analysts once pulled threads on stolen data, cross-checking corridor updates and ship manifests until their questions started drifting too close to someone's off-the-books routes. Whatever record survived will not be loud, just a buried file or half-archived trace that shows which jump patterns were nudged, when, and for whose benefit. A thousand tiny approvals, ignored discrepancies, and "temporary" fixes must have piled up in these systems until entire ships vanished off their own charts. So far the trail is a scrubbed slate on a lonely rock and scattered notes about disrupted theft chains, all pointing toward a navigator who has been working the gaps between what was reported and what really happened for far longer than anyone admitted.
zh: 在这里，那座研究舱安静地悬在几乎一无所有之上，正是官僚会遗忘、承包商会利用的那类地方。这里曾是分析员们追查被盗数据线索的地方，他们交叉核对走廊更新与船只舱单，直到自己的问题开始靠某人的账外航线太近。存活下来的任何记录都不会张扬，只是一份被埋的文件或半归档的痕迹，显示哪些跃迁模式被推动过、在何时、以及为了谁的利益。一千个微小的批准、被忽略的差异与"临时"修补，必然在这些系统里堆叠，直到整艘整艘的船从自己的星图上消失。目前为止，这条线索是一块孤独岩石上被擦净的数据板与关于被打断的盗窃链的零散笔记，全都指向一名领航员——他在"被报告的"与"真正发生的"之间的空档里运作的时间，比任何人承认的都长。

#en: The listening post sits at the edge of forgotten space, a rusting ear pointed toward the lanes long after its operators packed up and left, never bothering to ask what their machines kept hearing. The array buried here has been singing to itself for years, stitching together the subtle shoves and course corrections that turn routine jumps into slow-motion collisions, and the Salvage Crown Syndicate is only guarding it because they know anything this old and this secret has to be worth something. Whatever patterns have been recorded are anchored to this spot; pull them here and the whole map of nudged ships and curated wrecks shifts into focus. So far, all you have are a stray scrap of data from a backwater world and an abandoned relay humming with mismatched pings, both pointing to someone who started re-writing the lanes and then walked away before anyone understood what that would mean.
zh: 那座听音哨坐落在被遗忘太空的边缘，一只生锈的耳朵指向航道，而在它的操作员早已打包离开、从未费心问过他们的机器一直在听什么之后很久。埋在这里的阵列多年来一直在对自己歌唱，把那些把例行跃迁变成慢动作碰撞的细微推搡与航向修正缝在一起；"打捞王冠辛迪加"守着它，只是因为他们知道任何这么古老、这么隐秘的东西必然值点钱。被记录下的任何模式都锚定在这个点上；在这里把它们拉出来，那些被推动的船只与被策展的残骸的整张地图就会清晰起来。目前为止，你只有一穷乡世界上一块散落的数据碎片与一座嗡鸣着对不上脉冲的废弃中继，两者都指向某个开始改写航道、然后在任何人明白那意味着什么之前就走开的人。

#en: The automated harvesting platform drifts half-buried in the asteroid field, its cutters long silent, but its navigation spine still humming with course data no miner ever needed. This is where someone clever would hide a signal that piggybacks on routine telemetry, a quiet tug on any condemned ship routed along certain corridors, bending traffic toward the same patch of forgotten sky. The field itself keeps prying eyes away; only scavvers and the desperate risk threading these rocks, and even they give this hulk a wide berth without saying why. When the topic surfaces in mess halls and dock bars, the ones who work these lanes glance away, change subjects, pretend not to remember which wrecks vanished out here. So far the trail is a dead spacer's logs, a scrubbed patrol grid, and a deserter's stolen scans, all pointing to ships being steered off manifest into the dark by the same unseen hand.
zh: 那座自动化收割平台半埋在岩石场里漂着，它的切割臂早已沉默，可导航脊柱仍在嗡鸣着没有任何矿工需要的航向数据。这里正是某个聪明人会藏一道信号的地方——它搭在例行遥测的顺风车上，对任何沿特定走廊航行的报废船只轻轻一拽，把交通掰向同一片被遗忘的天空。岩石场本身挡住了窥探的眼睛；只有拾荒者与走投无路的人才冒险穿过这些岩石，而连他们都会不言原因地远远绕开这具残骸。当话题在食堂与码头酒吧浮现时，跑这些航道的人会移开目光、换个话题、假装不记得哪些残骸在这里消失。目前为止，这条线索是一块死掉太空劫匪的日志、一张被擦净的巡逻网格，以及一名逃兵偷来的扫描，全都指向船只在同一只无形之手的引导下被推出舱单、驶入黑暗。

#en: The orbit here is crowded with junk traffic and idle sats, a forgotten ring of hardware looping a world nobody bothers to check twice. That is precisely why the cache matters  a tiny misfiled update, some long-abandoned protocol left running on auto, and over time the system learned to route more and more course corrections through this one quiet lane. Now a lone escort, the ST-6273 Starblade, circles the clutter like it is guarding nothing at all, which makes it the most suspicious ship in local space. Somewhere in that tangle sits the key that links her hidden station to the rest of the grid.  \n\nSo far the trail runs from a stray dataslate on a backwater rock, through odd shipment timing flagged in farm logs, then into a dead relay still watching the skies on forgotten orders, each step revealing the same pattern of diverted routes and one navigator quietly bending traffic around herself.
zh: 这里的轨道挤满了废旧交通与闲置卫星，一圈被遗忘的硬件环绕着一颗没人费心复核两次的世界。这正是那处储藏点要紧的原因：一次微小的归档错误的更新、某个被遗弃后仍在自动运行的协议，久而久之，系统学会了把越来越多的航向修正经由这一条安静的航道。如今一艘单独的护航船，"ST-6273 星刃"，绕着那团杂物打转，像在守着一无所有——这让它成了本地区最可疑的飞船。在那团乱麻里某处，坐着那把把她隐藏的星际站与这张网格其余部分连起来的钥匙。  \n\n目前为止，线索从一穷乡岩石上一块散落数据板，穿过农场日志里被标记出来的古怪货运时机，然后钻进一座仍在按被遗忘命令注视着天空的死中继，每一步都揭示出同样的被改道航线模式，以及一名在自己周围悄悄掰弯交通的领航员。

#en: Only in high orbit does the pattern resolve: the beacon hangs in a thin sliver of space where grav readings slip between official survey grids, exactly the kind of blind angle a former stress analyst would trust more than any report. The Bloodwake holds position over it like a hired lock, Crimson Fleet gunners watching a prize they only half understand, guarding echoes of drive failures and lane distortions that have been traded as rumor and bar-talk so long the edges have worn smooth. Tapping this node here, at the point where his stolen models and real-space anomalies intersect, is the only way to separate myth from math and follow the chain back to its source. Up to now, the trail has been redacted incident logs in a quiet lab, frightened technicians hinting at tampered safety systems, and captains passing around distorted tales of a vanished analyst who keeps turning accidents into messages.
zh: 只有在高轨道，这个模式才清晰起来：那座信标悬在一条细狭的太空隙缝里，引力读数从官方勘探网格之间滑过——正是前应力分析员会信任甚于任何报告的盲角。"血尾流"像一把租来的锁般守在其上方，深红舰队的炮手看守着一件他们只懂一半的战利品，守着引擎故障与航道畸变的回声——它们被当作传闻与酒吧闲谈交易得太久，棱角都已磨平。在这里、在他被偷的模型与真实空间异常相交的节点上接入，是分辨神话与数学、并顺着链条追回源头的唯一办法。目前为止，这条线索是某间安静实验室里涂黑的事件日志、暗示安全系统被动手脚的受惊技师，以及船长们传述着关于一名失踪分析员的扭曲故事——他把事故不断变成信息。

#en: The Deimos yard is where old metal comes to be stripped of its identity, and that makes it the perfect place to hide a record no one wants to admit exists. Between rusted hull frames and half-gutted drive cores, the Hellbound Dustwalkers pick at whatever is left, selling stories about "bad jumps" and "cursed ships" to anyone who pays for drama, sanding the sharp edges off what really happened until it sounds like bar gossip instead of evidence. Somewhere under their grease-stained terminals and repurposed cores is the straight version, the one name and series of routes that keep showing up behind every quiet disaster. Up to now it is all been secondhand: a corrupted ping from a lonely outpost, a freighter log that did not match its manifest, a whispered account over cheap liquor in Neon and a half-joking warning from a freestar drifter about a hunter who follows broken drives instead of bounties.
zh: 火卫二场区，是旧金属被剥去身份的地方，这让它成了藏起一份"没人愿意承认存在之记录"的完美地点。在锈蚀的船壳框架与半掏空的引擎核心之间，地狱尘行者拾捡着剩下的东西，向任何愿意为戏剧性付钱的人兜售"坏跃迁"与"被诅咒的船"的故事，把真正发生之事磨平棱角，直到它听起来像酒吧闲话而非证据。在他们油污斑斑的终端与被改作他用的核心之下某处，是那个直白的版本：一个不断出现在每一场安静灾难背后的名字与一连串航线。到目前为止，全都是二手的：一座孤独前哨传来的损坏脉冲、一份与舱单不符的货船日志、霓虹城廉价烈酒间的一句低语，以及一名自由星系联盟流浪者关于"追着坏引擎而非赏金的猎人"的半开玩笑警告。

#en: The orbital-drop shelter is where the stories start overlapping, so if any place holds a trace of what really moved through those corridors, it is here among the scorched bulkheads and half-packed crates. Its battered consoles still hum with old traffic patterns, gaps and timing windows someone carved into the lanes and then tried to scrub away in a hurry. The liaison swore a navigator had threaded their runs through those gaps, but every retelling shifted a little: different rendezvous times, different exit points, always the same unseen hand. From manifests that do not balance at the mid-tier port, to a smuggler convoy that arrived early without extra burn, to whispers of charts marked with symbols no official route uses, every fragment points back to the same thing; someone is editing space itself, and this shelter is where their edits first brushed the people desperate enough to pay for them.
zh: 那座轨道投放掩体，正是故事开始重叠的地方；所以若有哪处保存着"真正穿过那些走廊的是什么"的痕迹，那就是这里——在烧焦的舱壁与半打包的箱子之间。它破损的控制台仍嗡鸣着旧交通模式，那些有人刻进航道、随后又匆忙试图擦掉的空缺与时机窗口。联络官发誓有一名领航员把他们的航次穿过了那些空缺，可每一次转述都稍有偏移：不同的会合时间、不同的出口点，永远是同一只看不见的手。从中间层港市对不上的舱单，到一支没额外点火却提前抵达的走私车队，再到关于"用任何官方航线都不用的符号标记星图"的低语，每一块碎片都指回同一件事：有人在编辑太空本身，而这座掩体正是他们的编辑最先触碰到那些绝望到愿意付钱之人的地方。

#en: The autonomous factory is the first place the numbers stopped adding up and the machines started whispering someone else's intent, which is why the file you are after would be buried here, half-forgotten in a system no one thinks to audit. Its guidance arrays sit at the crossroads of production and transit, where altered routes and stray rescue-frequency echoes can be dismissed as software noise, and where a mercenary outfit can loiter under contract cover without raising corporate alarms. Forward Shadowline holds this ground like they expect someone to come back for what was started in the diagnostics then abruptly abandoned mid-entry, a trail of half-written logs and rerouted shipments left hanging in mid-process. So far, all we have is a dead tech at a remote relay, a pattern of nudged shipping lanes, and scattered stories of a rescue pilot who always arrives just before the reports go missing.
zh: 那座自动化工厂是数字第一次不再对得上、机器开始低语别人意图的地方，这正是你要找的那份文件会被埋在这里的原因——半遗忘在一个没人想着去审计的系统里。它的制导阵列坐落在生产与运输的十字路口：在那里，被改动的航线与游离的救援频率回声都能被当作软件噪声打发；在那里，一支佣兵队伍能借合同掩护徘徊而不触发公司警报。"前锋暗影线"守在这片地面上，像在等着有人回来取那些在诊断中开始、随后又中途突然弃置的东西：一串写到一半的日志与被改道的货运，悬在流程中间。目前为止，我们只有一名死在远程中继的技师、一种被推动航运航道的模式，以及关于一名"总在报告消失之前恰好抵达"的救援飞行员零散的故事。

#en: Down here in Neon's Underbelly, nothing ever really leaves; it just seeps into the corners, into the pipes, into the people no one looks at twice. If someone wanted to bleed off the traces of bad jumps, scrub drive signatures and dump whatever a Grav core should never carry, it would end up in these channels, where runoff and secrets share the same conduits. The grid hums overhead, lights strobing through steam, and every maintenance hatch looks like it has not been opened in years, despite the warmth of recent work on the seals. This place has a habit of holding onto cargo, chems, even bodies longer than anyone planned, and the same goes for data ghosts. So far the trail has been a crooked line: a discarded slate on a forgotten rock, smeared beacon logs in lonely orbit, and a derelict Trade Authority hauler whose corrupted records all whisper the same name and point, again and again, toward Neon.
zh: 在霓虹城的下腹，没有什么东西真正离开过；它只是渗进角落、渗进管道、渗进那些没人会多看一眼的人里。若有人想把坏跃迁的痕迹放掉、擦净引擎签名、倾倒任何引力核心本绝不该携带的东西，它就会流进这些水道——径流与机密共用同一批管道。网格在头顶嗡鸣，灯光穿过蒸汽频闪，每一扇维护舱门看上去都像多年没开过，尽管密封圈上还有近期作业的余温。这地方有个习惯，会把货物、药剂、甚至尸体留得比任何人计划的都久，数据幽灵也一样。目前为止，这条线索是一条歪斜的线：被遗忘岩石上一块被丢弃的数据板、孤独轨道上被拖抹的信标日志，以及一艘损坏的贸易管理局货船——它损坏的记录全都低语着同一个名字，并一次又一次地指向霓虹城。

#en: Neon's rooftops are the only place he can see the whole grid he has been bending, a tangle of star lanes, corporate pads, and anonymous freighters lifting off into the storms beyond the Span. Up here, away from official flight control, Vector can patch directly into illicit nav buoys and shipboard relays, finalizing the jump lattice that will carry his most loyal captains beyond anyone's jurisdiction. If he finishes the work, his shadow routes harden into a permanent artery no faction can shut down without crippling their own traffic. A missed timestamp at a remote cache, a garbled Ryujin memo, and a SysDef analyst reading the wrong transponder log brought the trail here; a stolen dataslate in the hinterlands, quiet questions in a Neon tower, and a drifting tactical hull full of corrupted VectorSet runs all pointed to the same conclusion: someone has been rewriting how ships move through the dark.
zh: 霓虹城的屋顶，是他唯一能看清自己一直在掰弯的整张网格的地方：一团由星际航道、公司停机坪，以及升入桥架之外风暴的无名货船构成的乱麻。在这里，远离官方飞行控制，"向量"能直接接进非法导航浮标与船载中继，最终确定那张将把他最忠诚的船长们带出任何人管辖的跃迁网格。若他完成这项工作，他的影子航线就会硬化成一条任何派系都无法在不残废自身交通的情况下关闭的永久动脉。一处远程储藏点错过的时戳、一份乱码的龙神备忘录，以及一名读错应答器日志的星防队分析员，把线索带到了这里；腹地里一块被偷的数据板、霓虹城某座塔里安静的提问，以及一具塞满损坏 VectorSet 运行的漂移战术船壳，全都指向同一个结论：有人在改写船只如何在黑暗中移动。

#en: Out here, among rusted hulls and half gutted frames, Deadlock is surrounded by the language he understands best; every twisted beam and stripped Grav Drive mount is a tool he has already weighed and repurposed in his head. The abandoned Deimos scrapyard sits just far enough from official lanes for SysDef to look the other way, and close enough to old contracts that he can bleed value from forgotten war steel while he finishes what he started with those stolen schematics. If he is going to lock his story into place forever, burying evidence or rigging one last structural collapse to erase his part in the Vanguard disaster, it will be here, where corporate ledgers already read "written off." They counted on time and paperwork to smother this mess, but yard logs in a quiet corner, a runaway field tech in a buried bunker, and loose tongues in Gagarin Landing kept dragging his name back into circulation.
zh: 在这里，在锈蚀的船壳与被掏空一半的框架之间，"死锁"被他最了解的语言环绕；每一根扭曲的梁与每一个被剥光的引力引擎支架，都是他已在脑中称量并改作他用的工具。那座废弃的火卫二废料场离官方航道刚好足够远、让星防队转开视线，又离旧合同足够近、让他能在完成那些偷来的图纸所开始之事的同时从被遗忘的战争钢铁里榨取价值。若他要把自己的故事永久锁死——埋葬证据或策划最后一次结构坍塌来抹掉他在先锋队灾难中的角色——就会在这里，在公司账册早已写着"已核销"的地方。他们指望时间与文书闷死这摊烂局，可安静角落里的一份场区日志、一座被埋掩体里一名出走的战地技师，以及加加林着陆点里的碎嘴，都不断把他的名字拖回流言中。

#en: Out here, away from ports and patrol routes, the orbital lane is almost empty, which is exactly why this fragment of navigation data matters. No station traffic to muddy it, no civilian relays rewriting it for convenience; only raw vectors showing where the hidden tankers break from registered routes and vanish toward whatever off-grid cistern Catalyst favors. The RD-1964 Scrapviper circling this rock is not here by chance; someone paid Spacers to sit on these numbers and make sure no one compares them to what Cydonia and Neon keep on file. Some haulers swear they have seen ghost convoys peeling off into dark space, others shrug and say it is just spacer exaggeration. So far the trail runs from a dead relay sheltering bad manifests, through whispered complaints in Neon's underlevels, to mismatched cargo records at the mining hub, all pointing to a single hand quietly redrawing where the water flows.
zh: 在这里，远离港口与巡逻航线，那条轨道几乎空无一物，这正是这块导航数据值得在意的原因。没有星际站交通把它搅浑，没有民用中继为方便而改写它；只有赤裸的向量，显示那些隐藏的罐车在何处脱离登记航线、消失向"催化剂"偏爱的某座账外蓄水池。绕着这块岩石的"RD-1964 废料蝰蛇"不是偶然在此；有人付钱给太空劫匪，让他们盯着这些数字、确保没人把它们与赛多尼亚和霓虹城存档的内容比对。有些货船船工发誓见过幽灵车队脱离驶入黑暗太空，另一些人则耸肩说那不过是太空劫匪的夸张。目前为止，线索从一座庇护坏舱单的死中继，穿过霓虹城下城层里压低声音的抱怨，到采矿枢纽处对不上的货运记录，全都指向一只手在悄悄重画水流的方向。

#en: The retreat sits alone against the sky, a place people come to forget things and be forgotten in turn, which makes it the only fitting ground for a record that was never meant to survive. Its cabins and storm-scarred outbuildings shelter more ghosts than guests, and someone has threaded those ghosts into neat columns of names and dates, then cut the pages off where the stories turn ugly. Whatever was written here links the missing settlers, the quiet screenings, and that soft-voiced courier whose trail never quite lines up, but whole segments of memory feel shaved away, like everyone present agreed which parts would never be spoken of. So far the trail is simple on paper and twisted in the telling: a stray slate on a dead rock, altered logs in a backline clinic, a medic who remembered a Belizean accent, and an old missioner who kept careful lists of people who met the same woman and never came home.
zh: 那座隐居地孤零零地倚着天空，一个人们来此遗忘事情、也反过来被遗忘的地方——这让它成了唯一适合存放一份"本不该存活之记录"的地面。它的木屋与布满风暴伤痕的附属建筑庇护的幽灵比客人还多，而有人把那些幽灵穿成了整齐的名字与日期之列，然后在故事变丑的地方把书页剪掉。在这里写下的无论什么，都把失踪的定居者、安静筛查，以及那名行踪总对不上的柔和嗓音信使系在一起，可整段整段的记忆感觉被削掉了，仿佛在场所有人都同意哪些部分将永不被提起。目前为止，这条线索在纸面上简单、在转述中扭曲：死岩石上一块散落数据板、后方诊所里被改动的日志、一名记得伯利兹口音的医疗兵，以及一名仔细列出"见过同一个女人、再没回家的人"的老传教士。

#en: If she has been feeding altered routes into the lanes, the only place to catch the pattern clean is at the heart of sanctioned traffic, where every freighter, courier, and shadow-run must file a story about how it came and went. New Atlantis hums with official versioned truth, but in its freight offices and backroom berths the real paths are whispered, sold, and quietly forgotten as long as the cargo keeps flowing. Buried among routine manifests and hushed arguments over who took which shortcut, there will be one thread that repeats the same off-lane approach too many times to be coincidence, a line no one will admit to plotting but everyone seems to have used. So far the trail is a stray dataslate on a backwater world, wreck reports from vanished settlers, and salvaged records from a stripped-out yard, all hinting that someone has been bending the safe corridors away from where the maps say they go.
zh: 若她一直在把被改动的航线喂进航道，那唯一能干净捕捉到这个模式的地方，就是获批交通的心脏——在那里，每一艘货船、信使船与影子航次都必须提交一份关于它如何来去的说法。新亚特兰蒂斯城嗡鸣着官方的版本化真相，但在它的货运办公室与后室泊位里，真正的路径被低语、被买卖、被悄悄遗忘——只要货物继续流动。埋在例行舱单与关于"谁抄了哪条近路"的低声争吵之间，会有一根线把同一种偏航进近重复太多次、无法当作巧合：一条没人愿意承认自己绘过、却似乎人人都用过的线。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡世界上一块散落数据板、失踪定居者的残骸报告，以及一座被剥光场区里打捞出的记录，全都暗示有人一直在把安全走廊掰离星图所指之处。
